title: The Carbon Cycle
seo_title: Year 9 Science: The Carbon Cycle Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Represent the carbon cycle and examine how key processes including combustion, photosynthesis and respiration rely on interactions between Earth's spheres (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on the carbon cycle: carbon stores, photosynthesis, respiration, combustion, decomposition, ocean uptake, fossil fuels and CO₂ data. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Photosynthesis takes CO₂ out of the air; respiration, combustion and decay put it back.
body_html:
How to think about it

Carbon cycles between the air, living things, oceans and rocks.

  • Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (removes CO₂ from the air).
  • Respiration, decomposition and combustion return CO₂ to the air.
  • Burning fossil fuels moves carbon stored for millions of years back into the air faster than it is removed.
Example

A tree grows 50 kg heavier. Where did the carbon come from?

photosynthesis uses CO₂ from air

Answer: the air

Example

Coal is burnt. Which store gains carbon?

combustion releases CO₂

Answer: the atmosphere

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their carbon from the soil.
  • Thinking only animals respire.
  • Thinking carbon is destroyed when fuel burns.

faq.q: Why is the carbon cycle important?
faq.a: It moves carbon between living things and the environment. The balance of carbon dioxide in the air affects Earth's temperature.

faq.q: How do humans change the carbon cycle?
faq.a: Burning fossil fuels and clearing forests add carbon dioxide to the air faster than plants and oceans can remove it.
A store that takes in more carbon than it gives out, such as a growing forest, seagrass meadow or the ocean.
